articleTitle: Creation of digital twins of neural network technology of personalization of food products for diabetics
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The article discusses the problems of creating Digital Twin for use in neural network technology for personalizing food products for people with a genetic predisposition to diabetes. When designing an information system for personalizing food products, it is proved that the main direction of development is the modeling of a Digital Twin of the product and the consumer, as well as the determination of the technologies that form the basis of the personalized food model to create an accurate, correctly functioning system.

articleTitle: On Real Queue Length in a Queueing System with Erlang-r service time
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a system, which, according to the Kendall classification, is denoted by M/E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>/1. The article is also dedicated to one of the approaches of studying the systems that do not have Markov property. For one of these system the main characteristics are given and, in addition, for the first time the concept of a real queue is considered. The relevance of this study is determined by the wide use of such models in the industrial engineering and traffic engineering problems. A description of the construction of a simulation model in the AnyLogic system is given, the main characteristics are calculated and compared with the results of analytical modeling.

articleTitle: Comparison of Personality Recognition Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Automation of document circulation is becoming more and more relevant every day. Today, it is difficult to imagine life without the Internet, as a result of which enterprises develop and the need for personal identification grows without leaving home. Personal identification is used in many areas (banking, electronic payment systems, forensics, etc.). To simplify the verification process, many businesses are switching to identity verification by providing personal information and photographs of identity documents. The relevance of the study is due to the growing need to simplify and improve the accuracy of personal identification by providing photographs of documents and personal data. The aim of the work is to analyze existing algorithms for recognizing text and faces in an image.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Dynamic Analysis of Non-Contact Atomic Force Microscope
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: This work aims to construct a mathematical model to investigate the dynamical behavior of cantilever of the atomic force microscope in the non-contact working state. To create the model of the cantilever lumped parameter model is utilized. In this work, to model the tip-sample interaction force we use the Van der Waals force. This external force makes the system nonlinear. To solve the system, and obtaining the frequency response equation, the Van der Pol averaging method is utilized. The effect of the non-linearity, the excitation amplitude, and the damping coefficient on the frequency response equation of the system are studied.

articleTitle: Emergence of complicated regular and irregular spontaneous Ca2+ oscillations in astrocytes
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the transitions between various spontaneous activity modes observed in astrocyte. In order to describe the cell's behavior, the calcium concentrations in the cytosol and in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and change in IP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> concentration in the cell were considered. The impact of various calcium flows between the cytosol and the endoplasmic reticulum as well as role of the production process in IP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> formation, were studied.

articleTitle: Integration technology for replacing damaged brain areas with artificial neuronal networks
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We present a novel integration technology for replacing damaged microcircuits in the rat brain with electronic neuronal networks. This technology will allow simulating important brain functions, such as memory, through the adaptive stimulating effects of neural interfaces at cellular and neuronal network levels. The proposed system includes electronic devices to register and process neuronal signals and to adaptively stimulate damaged brain areas according to the online algorithm decoding the registered neuronal activity. The stimulation algorithm is implemented in hardware neural network with memristive connections that allows both network learning and adaptive re-learning.The basic idea is to develop components of hardware neural network with memristive connections for adaptive generation of electrical signals to stimulate particular brain areas. Moreover, the uniqueness of the system is adaptive closed-loop connection between two hippocampal neuronal networks. Such a system is very promising for restoring functionality of damaged areas in the human brain to replace lost functions in patients with brain pathologies or trauma.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach for Tensegrity Form Finding: Feature Extraction Problem
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of form finding for a tensegrity structure with the use of a machine learning pipeline, including feature extraction and regression, is studied. Tensegrity robots present a range of new opportunities in a number of areas in robotics, however the lack of efficient and scalable tools for controlling their motion slows down their deployment. This study aims to add a new tool for solving one of the basic problems encountered in tensegrity robot control: finding a stable equilibrium state (and its inverse task). Using machine learning approach makes the solution scalable and potentially faster than iterative optimization-based methods. The paper provides a view into the issue of feature extraction, and provides implementation of a number of feature extraction methods: Principle Component Analysis (PCA), Kernel PCA, undercomplete, denoising and sparse autoencoders.

articleTitle: Antilock braking system fuzzy controller optimization with a genetic algorithm in a form of cellular automaton
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: This paper is devoted to the issue of efficient and intuitive visualization of optimization processes. The problem is considered on the example of ground wheeled vehicle antilock braking system fuzzy control element optimization using a genetic algorithm in the form of a cellular automaton.

articleTitle: The results of modeling electrical processes in low-temperature plasma modification of metal surfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The results of modeling electrical processes that occur during low-temperature plasma modification of metal surfaces using the model developed by the authors are presented. The main regularities of the influence of operating parameters (the magnetron anode current and the potential supplied to the product), product parameters and the product surface layer characteristics on the behavior of the electric signal have been identified.

articleTitle: Using neural network to ensure the packing quality of pasteurized milk
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The article considers the application of the neural network model to check the quality of packaging of drinking milk in the technological production process. The neural network allows you to remove the routine load from the verification staff. Method of detection of possible defective areas and identification of signs of damage of packing areas is used. Experiments have shown that when using the proposed solution in production - the accuracy indicator can exceed 80%. Detecting scrap on a conveyor belt in order to detect objects of a certain class is one of the most complex branches of computer vision. Methods of existing standard detection models were analyzed, with the development of which the performance of deep learning networks was significantly improved. An overview of systematic object detection methods covering single-stage and two-stage detectors is provided. Use of these methods of object detection for creation of efficient neural network technology is considered.

articleTitle: The Effect Of Virtual Reality On Mental Health In The Design Of Automated Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The article provides an integrated analysis of practical application of virtual reality (VR) in healthcare. Modern VR products have been created for the diagnosis and treatment of post-traumatic syndrome, Alzheimer’s disease, alcohol dependence, phobic disorders, and teenage depression. Information on such products is limited to simple scenes, without adaptation to the user. The paper shows a prospect for creating a virtual system with biological feedback. The proposed system is a set of portable and stationary devices for recording physiological signals and immersion into a virtual reality environment, as well as smart nodes for registration, processing and decision-making to correct the user’s mental state.

articleTitle: Modern approaches to the formation of intelligent monitoring in the context of digital manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The paper investigates current approaches to intelligent monitoring in digitalization of multiproduct automated manufacturing and gives an example of monitoring the quality of manufactured parts based on neural networks.

articleTitle: Processing Electronic Nose Data Using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We investigate the qualitative and quantitative analysis of gas mixtures using semiconductor metal oxide sensors. This analysis can be performed using multi-sensor systems at a constant temperature or using single-sensor systems at a variable temperature. The latter method is more reliable and efficient, but requires advanced statistical analysis of multidimensional data. Using pre-trained artificial neural networks allowed us not only to recognize analytes with reliability close to 100%, but also to determine their volume concentration with an error not exceeding 15%.

articleTitle: Influence of Vibrotactile Feedback on the Motor Evoked Potentials (MEPs) Induced by Motor Imagery
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Motor imagery brain-computer interface (MI BCI) is a rapidly developing method of rehabilitation after a stroke. The presence of feedback is an essential point in closing the disturbed sensorimotor loop for the patients. In this work, we investigate motor cortex excitability changes after training with BCI, resulting in motor evoked potentials (MEPs). Seven healthy subjects took part in three experimental conditions: I) direct vibrotactile feedback while training; II) control session with constant vibration; III) BCI training without feedback Special attention was paid to classification accuracy, degree of desynchronization, and MEP measurements. The study has shown that the absence of the feedback does not influence the classification accuracy. The desynchronization degree was significantly higher (p<; 0,05) for all the subjects in the experiments with the feedback, meanwhile, there was no significant difference in MEPs.

articleTitle: Short-term memory in neuron-astrocyte network
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In this paper, we study the role of astrocyte-induced modulation of signal transmission in network of synaptically coupled spiking neurons in the mechanisms of the short-term memory formation. We show, that due to the local spatial synchronization of signaling in the neural network induced by the astrocyte during the duration of the Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> signal, the proposed neuron-astrocyte network can operate as a temporal Hopfield network.

articleTitle: Classification of external signal by spiking neural network of bistable Hodgkin-Huxley neurons
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We propose a classifier consisting of Hodgkin-Huxley neurons based on the activation of a different number of neurons depending on the external current amplitude. We consider a network with 2 output neurons and train the classifier for 2 external current pulses with different amplitudes by adaptation of the couplings between neurons of the main network and the output neurons.

articleTitle: Oscillations of synchronization in inhibitory coupled Hodgkin-Huxley neurons network
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of complex network of Hodgkin-Huxley neurons. It consists of 3 sub-networks. The first small network receives external signal which is transferred into a spike sequence. Then it is transmitted to two small-world networks interacting via an inhibitory coupling and working together to process the signal. We observe that the synchronization index (SI) in both networks periodically changes in time: the time intervals with the high SI alternate with the time intervals where SI is low. We calculate correlation between them and find that when adjusting the strength of the inhibitory coupling one can observe SI in these networks changes either in phase or out of phase.

articleTitle: Study of Voiced Speech Using Empirical Mode Decomposition to Detect Stressful Emotions in Human-Robot Interaction
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: A method for studying voiced speech by means of improved complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise to detect stressful emotions in human-robot interaction is presented. The informative parameters of voiced speech fully reflect the violation in functioning of organs of human speech apparatus due to emotional excitation. The key feature of the research is to decompose a signal into empirical modes, to detect modes containing periodic information on the excitation source of the vocal tract, and to construct a composite signal reflecting information on glottal activity. The research results of voiced speech, being computation of the fundamental frequency of 100 multi-harmonic signals, are presented. The pitch frequency modulation of multi-harmonic signals in the frequency range of 0-2.5 Hz/ms in 0.5 Hz/ms increments simulated the irregularity in vibration of the vocal folds (30-40 % of the nominal value) arising from the emotional excitation of a person. The results obtained allow us to conclude that the presented method for the study of voiced speech, using the improved decomposition, can be successfully tested to detect stressful emotions in human interaction with robotic devices.

articleTitle: Quantum Computation by Classical Mechanical Apparatuses
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We design a mechanical apparatus that works as "quantum" computer even though it follows classical physics. To do quantum computation, we need to know what percentage of a particular state is included in a superposed quantum state. However, the superposition easily breaks unless expensive and large-scale tooling, such as cryogenic temperature is prepared. We pay attention to causal formulation of quantum mechanics. The weighting coefficients of the superposition can be determined by monitoring the trajectory of a quantum particle. Such monitoring is possible only in macroscopic physics. Efficacy of our macroscopic apparatus model is shown in one of typical quantum algorithms, Deutsch algorithm. This classical mechanical design opens the way for "quantum mechanical" artificial intelligence to be mounted on robots in usual macroscopic world.

articleTitle: Spatial memory based on an STDP-driven neural network
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We propose a model of spatial memory implemented in a Spiking Neural Network (SNN) and test it on a robot moving in an environment with neutral and harmful regions. Neurons in the SNN play the role of place cells, and their population dynamics determines the robot movements. We show that STDP rearranges the couplings in the SNN and forms spatial memory similar to cognitive maps associated with the negative experience. Then, the robot learns to avoid harmful zones.

articleTitle: Synchronization in two-layer networks of chaotic oscillators via a double distributed control
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In some of the real-world networks, the interacting agents synchronize in groups or clusters, not in a complete way; and also, many networks can be modeled by multi-layer networks where nodes are coupled in several independent networks. In this work, we deal with the problem of synchronizing a pair of layers of networks via a double distributed control. Specifically, these controllers depends on the degree of nodes. Our first aim is synchronizing just some nodes of each layer, and then as a second goal, we apply a control to the already synchronized nodes of each layer to assure that they follow the same dynamics in both layers.

articleTitle: The Respiratory Organs Effect on Hemodynamics Evaluating Method Based on Hydro-Cuff Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The method development is explained by the need to assess the respiratory organs influence degree on hemodynamics informative indicators and pulse wave forms. This method implementation in practical health care will solve a number of early diagnosis problems of socially significant diseases. It is proposed to use hydro-cuff for obtaining pulse waves. This technology significantly increases pulse wave curve perception sensitivity. The method will increase the pulse wave contour representation reliability, as a result, it will increase the hemodynamic parameters estimation accuracy by removing the respiratory component. It will expand the functionality of systems, devices and complexes that implement non-invasive methods for evaluating cardiovascular pathologies. It will make it possible to develop supporting mechanism for diagnosing respiratory diseases.

articleTitle: Route to Coherence in a Frequency-Heterogeneous Kuramoto Network
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Synchronization phenomena in populations of interacting elements are the subject of extensive research in biological, chemical, physical and social systems. Understanding of the emergent behavior in controlled experiments or real systems requires a focus on the consideration of heterogeneous network models. In this study, we explore the influence of the network topology on the rout to coherence in a heterogeneous Kuramoto model under the monotonically increasing coupling strength. Specifically, we consider regular (non-locally coupled ring), small-world (SW) and scale-free (SF) networks. We demonstrate a specific type of a chimera-like behavior that emerges in all three types of topology under certain conditions.

articleTitle: Motor Control: Neurophisiological Basis and BCI Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: This report is devoted to the review of the modern state-of-art of human motor control studies. We discuss the main neuronal processes that accomplished both the motor initiation phase and motor task execution. We also consider the possibility of creating brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) for neurorehabilitation of the motor skills of the patients after strokes and brain injuries. Finally, age-related changes in the human brain motor system functioning are considered.

articleTitle: Analysis of the features of brain neuronal sources during imagery motor activity: MEG study
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We analyzed the features of motor imagery (imagery arms movements) in the source level, applying the Dynamic Imaging of Coherent Sources method to MEG signals. We obtained the results that have confirmed the existence of two types of motor imagery: visual imagery and kinesthetic imagery. We have analyzed averaged distributions of normalized sources power for the visual imagery and kinesthetic imagery subgroups of volunteers and identified the main differences between these types of motor imagery in terms of the excitation of sources of neural activity.

articleTitle: Modern research on the primary school children brain functioning in the learning process
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The article deals with research related to the study of the primary school children's brain activity in the educational process: the prevalence of such research, the definition of the scientists' activities main directions on the topic and their chosen approaches to research. Conclusions about the need for further study of this issue are presented.

articleTitle: Comparing Spectral Properties Of Finger Photoplethysmography Signals In Healthy Subjects And Arterial Hypertension Patients
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The paper compares autonomic activity of healthy subjects and patients with hypertension. To estimate the autonomic activity in both groups we accessed the following spectral characteristics of finger photoplethysmogram: power density in low-frequency (LF%) and high-frequency (HF%) ranges in relation to total power in 0-0.4 frequency band, and sympathovagal balance (LF%/HF%). The comparison revealed statistically significant increase of HF%, decrease of LF% as well as decrease in LF%/HF% both in male and female hypertensive patients. Obtained results suggested that spectral characteristics of finger photoplethysmogram can be used as indexes of hypertension in sub-clinical stage.

articleTitle: Bistable tori and long transient dynamics in three coupled identical ring oscillators
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: On the example of three coupled identical ring oscillators, the coexistence of two stable homogeneous tori embedded in each other, corresponding to the regimes of successive activity of oscillators, is established. It is shown that a small stable torus is born from a stable periodic regime as a result of supercritical Neirmark-Sacker bifurcation. A large torus is formed as a result of saddle-node bifurcation. We present a study of the formation of tori coexistence as well as long transient dynamics on the threshold of bistability.

articleTitle: Comparison of methods of quantitative analysis of phase synchronization according to test data modeling non-stationary signals of biological nature
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: A comparison is made of the methods for studying the phase synchronization of strongly unsteady systems. Methods were compared in the analysis of artificial test data modeling non-stationary signals of biological nature. The range of free parameters of the methods is determined, which ensures the best sensitivity and specificity of the methods.

Author Keywords: autonomous regulation of heart rhythm and mean blood pressure

articleTitle: Phase Dynamics Based and Spectral Charateristics of Directional Couplings in Ensemble of Three Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The problem of directional coupling detection in ensembles of temporally evolving systems from observed time series is important in diverse fields. A small ensemble of three oscillators is a model of large ensembles which carry important features such as the distinction between direct and indirect influences and, therefore, allows the study of the methods for coupling detection in respect of their ability to distinguish between such influences and, hence, correctly identify directional couplings and provide their appropriate quantitative description. This work considers an ensemble of three exemplary oscillators as a test system to improve the coupling estimation method based on phase dynamics modeling and compare it to the spectral approach called Granger - Geweke spectrum. Possibilities of false conclusions about the structure of couplings are analyzed, sensitivity of both methods and interpretations of coupling characteristics are discussed.

articleTitle: Applicability of correlation analysis for dynamic detection of single cancer cells with photoacoustic technique
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In many cases, cancers are detected only after they have become untreatable due to development of deadly metastasis. Most treatment is more effective at early cancer stages. We explore early cancer diagnosis at singe cell levels by their irradiation with short laser pulses followed by time-resolved detection of laser-induced acoustic waves. We explored the viability of correlation analysis for analysis of acoustic responses. It was estimated that correlation between cancer cells responses is 0.86±0.06, while correlation between cancer cells responses and responses from human blood is - 0.05±0.06.

articleTitle: Dynamical analysis of the neural and equilibrium seeking movement activity
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: This work is devoted to the study of the process of maintaining equilibrium in an experiment with a balance platform. The conducted experiment is very original in comparison with similar experiments conducted using stabilized platforms with remote control due to the presence of active feedback from the subject. We have analyzed the effect of learning from session to session during the experiment. We observe the changes in the patterns of electrical activity of the brain that occurred at the time of equilibrium for the main EEG activity frequency ranges.

articleTitle: On including the CA in polyimides polymerization modeling
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The article considers the possibility of including a cellular automaton in the model of polyimide polymerization process. Given the demand for the synthesis of new polyimide compounds, the problem of mathematical modeling of polyimide polymers becomes urgent. Based on the representation of chemical reactions as a dynamic process, an assumption is made about the adequacy of the use of cellular automaton model.

articleTitle: Russia in the 20-21 century: mathematical modeling based on the socio-energy approach
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The article is devoted to modeling the socio-political development of Russia in 1910-2009 based on the author's socio-energy approach. In this paper, we briefly talk about the basics of the proposed approach, its principles and basic equations. Based on them, computer modeling is carried out and the characteristic regularity of the development of society in Russia in 1910-2009 is derived.

articleTitle: Modeling spike and wave discharge initiation, maintenance and termination with hierarchical networks of neurooscillators
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Here we propose the network model of spike and wave discharges (SWDs) composed of four populations of neurooscillators representing pyramids, interneurons, thlamo-cortical cells and cells of reticular thalamic nucleus. Nervus trigeminus is considered as an external exciting input for the thalamo-cortical population. First, a simple network of 14 neurons is investigated and possible bifurcation mechanisms leading to SWD development is revealed. Then a larger network of 500 cells is considered reproducing the same mechanism. We show that SWDs can be described as a long transient process rather than a stable regime.

articleTitle: Space-charge-limited current in an external magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: This work is devoted to the study of one of the fundamental properties of the beam, namely, space-charge-limited current in a cylindrical drift tube located in an external magnetic field of various intensities. The value of the external magnetic field is determined for different beam energies, at which a sharp change in the critical current and beam dynamics occurs.

articleTitle: Room for doubt as a way to improve the accuracy of machine learning algorithms
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The decision-making process in diagnostics can be mitigated if an abstinence option is provided in a machine learning algorithm. This option may reduce false prediction possibility. Design of such an algorithm is associated with two difficulties: how to train a program to have some doubts and how to overcome those doubts? This paper deals with pneumonia detection task using a chest x-ray images dataset. Cropping an image into fragments, then classification of these cropped images into "normal", "pneumonia" and "abstain" classes, and then making a general diagnosis based on partial diagnosis for all image fragments allow accuracy improvement compared to the diagnosis of the whole image classified into the "normal" and "pneumonia" classes.

articleTitle: Estimating elementary cognitive functions based on EEG signals analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Human performance in complex mental tasks relies on elementary cognitive abilities, e.g., information processing speed and working memory capacity. These elementary functions can be measured on a behavioral level using elementary tasks, e.g., reaction time and memory scanning tasks. Cognitive and behavioral neuroscience aims to reveal cortical activity features underlying human performance in the elementary cognitive tasks. In this work, we designed a reaction time task based on the processing of ambiguous sensory stimuli. We found a correlation between the task performance on the behavioral level and the sensor-level cortical activity.

articleTitle: Database for storing and organizing data of neurophysiological experiments: description and basic functionality
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In present paper, we introduce a database containing multichannel experimental data of brain electrical activity (M/EEG signals) supplemented by necessary experimental protocols and additional characteristics of the subject (ECG, EOG, EMG, etc.), as well as the results of various processing methods application to the initial data. Data management and access is implemented with web-interface containing the toolkit for viewing and editing existing data and adding new items. Developed database provides increased level of data storage reliability and instant access to the neurophysiological data for analysis, processing and evaluation of accumulated experimental information.

articleTitle: The activity of the brain cortical network during solving tasks
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the functional connectivity between changes in the concentration of oxyhemoglobin, deoxyhemoglobin, and total hemoglobin, recorded by various leads of fNIRS from the frontal and parietal cortex. The obtained coefficients characterizing the functional connectivity between a pair of leads were presented in the form of a matrix. We analyzed the changes in functional connectivity during the performance of the subject of simple cognitive tasks associated with spatial perception.

articleTitle: Mobile robot control system
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The growth of robotics in Russia and in the world has recently increased the level of entry into the field of robotics, broadens its field of knowledge, and in this regard, the level of requirements for robotic systems, including control systems, is growing. This article discusses the control system of a mobile robot based on the Atmega microcontroller, presents its schematic diagram, and the operation algorithm. In addition, the electrical circuit of the platform is considered, the interaction scheme of the Atmega controller and the NVIDIA single-board computer is described. The main problems arising in the design of mobile robots are analyzed, the ways of their solution are proposed. This article may be of interest to centers of technical creativity, specialists in the field of robotics and mechatronics, as well as teams leading the preparation for the global Robomaster competition.

articleTitle: Automating of process design of robotic multiproduct machine-building complexes based on formalization of design procedures for analysis of requirements for assembly of high-precision products
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The article considers the issue of enlarged block of design procedures of analyzing requirements of assembly of high-precision products of the system of accounting requirements for the assembly in the design of manufacturing methods of machining. The proposed modernization will allow to more efficiently perform of the design dimensional analysis of a high-precision assembly unit in an automated fashion and choose rational manufacturing methods of machining of parts during process design of the production of robotic multinomenclature machine building complexes.

articleTitle: Analysis of multilayer perceptron based approach in studying brain neuronal connectivity networks
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In this paper, we present an analysis of modern tools for processing brain neuronal connectivity graphs - feed-forward artificial neural network. Different configurations of multilayer perceptron were considered and tested against an inference of functional dependence in model systems, specifically on Rossler oscillators generated data. Graphs of training, test and dynamics were considered. Furthermore, analysis and comparison of the r-squared scores and executed time were collected to measure the efficiency of the configurations.

articleTitle: Assessment of diffusion-kinetic and thermodynamic characteristics of Al-Pr-H alloy obtained by the method of cathodic incorporation
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The results of a study of temperature impact on the diffusion-kinetic and thermodynamic formation characteristics of Al-Pr-H electrode are presented. With an increase in the electrolyte temperature, an increase in the diffusion-kinetic characteristics occurs, namely, the rate constant, current density at the time of activation, diffusion rate, and hydrogen adsorption value.

articleTitle: The influence of the photoplethysmographic sensors passband to the possibility of analyzing of low-frequency processes of autonomic control
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We developed a digital broadband finger photoplethysmogram (PPG) sensor and compared its characteristics with a standard certified PPG recorder. During testing, we recorded the frequency responses (FR) of the sensors, and also compared the spectrums of the PPG signals recorded synchronously. An example of a system based on a microcontroller is also given, with the helped to record PPG signal. The study is important for understanding the influence of the passband of the PPG sensor and the bit depth of the analog-to-digital converter (ADC) of PPG sensor on the possibility of analyzing the synchronization of low-frequency processes of autonomic regulation.

articleTitle: Sensor Data Compression for the Normal Reaction Predictor Training for Walking Robots
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of compression and feature extraction for walking robot sensor data is studied. The aim is to facilitate the process of building a machine learning-based predictor for the ground reaction forces, which should allow to simplify generating control systems for walking robots, capable of working in changing contact interaction scenarios. In particular, the paper proposes use of undercomplete and overcomplete autoencoders for an automated feature extraction, with the aim of using the encoders as a preprocessing step in the machine learning (ML)-based ground reaction predictor, implemented by solving a regression problem. Papers shows trends in the mean squared error (MSE) on reconstruction tasks for different depths and structures of the encoders, demonstrates the trade-off between complexity and the quality of the reconstruction.

articleTitle: Hyperchaotic pseudohyperbolic attractors and quasiattractors in minimal ensembles of oscillators
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We present a study of two minimal ensembles of oscillators of principally different types. The first ensemble describes the dynamics of two coupled classical Lorenz system. We demonstrate that it can generate robust chaotic dynamics associated with pseodohyperbolic attractors by Turaev-Shilnikov. The second ensemble describes dynamics of two coupled generators of quasiperiodic oscillations. It exhibits non-robust chaotic dynamics associated with quasiattractors of Afraimovich-Shilnikov type. Hyperchaotic dynamics are shown for both types of ensembles. Characteristic structures of parameter planes are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Classification of hand-related real and imaginary motor activity with fNIRS
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In the present work we studied blood oxygenation/deoxygenation spatial dynamics related to real and imaginary motor activity using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). We revealed biomarkers based on pronounced hemispheric lateralization of hemodynamical response in the motor cortex during motor activity. We used these markers to design a sensing method for classification of movement's type. The accuracy of real movements classification was close to 100%, while for imaginary movements it was lower but still quite high (about 90%). The proposed system can find application, for example, in neurorehabilitation after severe brain injuries, including traumas and strokes.

articleTitle: The Role of Astrocytic Gap Contacts on Spontaneous Bioelectrical Activity of Neuronal Networks In Vitro
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Features of neuronal networks activity in primary hippocampal cultures under acute and chronic blockade of astrocytic gap contacts (connexins 43) have been studied. Primary hippocampal cells were obtained from murine embryonic tissue and cultured on multielectrode arrays (MEA60). The studies revealed the modulation of spontaneous bioelectrical activity characterized by a decrease of network burst activity and changes in the burst activation patterns. Moreover, chronic blockade of connexins 43 completely eliminated the network burst activity beginning on the third day after treatment.

articleTitle: Cloning of Chimera States in a Network of Bistable Time-Delayed Feedback Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The collective dynamics in a multiplex network of identical oscillators with time-delayed feedback is studied. In the numerical simulation, we demonstrate a new effect, named as cloning of chimera states. We have shown that this cloning occurs as a result of dynamics competition between the pairs of oscillators from different layers, but not due to the synchronization of oscillators.

articleTitle: Gross rate of productivity computerized manufacturing systems based on the innovation of the control-and-measuring’s choice
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Article presented the approach for improve the efficiency of computerized production systems, based on the use of an efficient kit of control-and-measuring tools in the technological processes for manufacturing products, using modern technological robotic equipment.

articleTitle: Robust Localization of a Self-Driving Vehicle in a Lane
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Localization is still one of the most challenging tasks in autonomous driving on city roads. Further development and improvement of automatic functions of vehicles in urban conditions are not possible without overcoming the problem of significant degradation of GNSS signal quality. The proposed approach to localization can provide information about vehicle position on the road in different operational conditions. Desired stability and quality are achieved by using the combination of conventional computer vision, neural networks and Kalman filtering.

articleTitle: Consequence Development Analysis as a Result of Cyberattacks on a Technological Complex with Variable-Frequency Drives
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Modern frequency converters for the electric drive have a built-in RS485 data transfer interface with Modbus protocol allowing remote configuration and diagnostics. In this case, there is a possibility of unauthorized access to the frequency converter settings, resulting in the emergency occurrence. This problem requires a detailed study of the processes that can be occurred as a cyberattack result on technological complexes with variable-frequency drive. The article considers this problem aspects applying to the system providing the necessary temperature regime for the main gas transport.

articleTitle: Chaos and hyperchaos in the chain of quantum coherent elements
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We study the chain of coupled quantum coherent systems with energy pumping and dissipation. Examples of such systems include the coupled Rydberg atoms with laser driving and spontaneous emission or electromagnetically driven artificial qubits with decoherence and dissipation. We found out that such system is able to demonstrate spontaneous onset of chaotic and even hyperchaotic oscillations, which are characterized by one or several positive Lyapunov exponents. Remarkably, the number of the positive Lyapunov exponents grows with the number of the chain elements. Hence a large chain is able to demonstrate highly irregular behavior. We investigate transition from regular to chaotic behavior and reveal the related instabilities.

articleTitle: Parameter identification of a class of nonlinear systems with structure uncertainly using controlled symmetric motions
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: This paper proposes the generalization of the nonlinear models for which the identification method based on symmetric motions can be applied with high efficiency. We chose two symmetric motion intervals which helps to simplify the calculations. We also propose a new iterative-adaptive algorithm for a high accuracy tracking control. Based on the symmetry criteria we iteratively calculate estimations and use them in the control algorithm.

articleTitle: Detecting inter-areal functional connectivity using artificial neural network
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In present paper we introduce an extended machine-learning-based approach to detect inter-areal functional connectivity based on artificial neural network (ANN). We prove the efficiency of the proposed method by applying multi-layer perceptron to find functional relations between the cortex and thalamus of the pathological WAG/Rij rats during the epileptic seizure based on the multivariate electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings. We show that the proposed algorithm is able to reconstruct the increased coupling within a thalamo-cortical network during the seizure versus a baseline activity.

articleTitle: Impact of the steady state IP3 level on the intracellular Ca2+ signaling in spatially distributed model of astrocyte
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The functional role of calcium signaling in astrocytic remains actively debated. One of the main reasons for such a debate is that the astrocytic calcium dynamics are characterized by high spatiotemporal complexity, which was confirmed by new high resolution imaging techniques. Another reason was the evidence of bi-directional astrocytic regulation of neuronal activity referred as gliotransmission. The biophysical mechanisms of spatiotemporal calcium dynamics in astrocytic are still incompletely clear. In this work we propose detailed multi-compartmental model of calcium signaling in astrocytic process. The model of each compartment describes the spontaneous dynamics of intracellular calcium concentration induced by the calcium entry to the cytosol through plasma membrane from the extracellular space. Compartments are coupled through the diffusion of Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> and IP3. Model represents basic principles of generation and propagation of calcium patterns in spatially distributed structure of astrocytic process. We have investigated the effect of the steady state level of intracellular IP3 concentration on the Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> dynamics in the process. It was shown that the sizes, durations and frequencies of these local calcium waves are directly proportional to the IP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> concentration.

articleTitle: Phase analysis of long-term signals by determining the protophase and phase of the signal
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In this paper, we investigated two methods for determining instantaneous phases using long-term recordings of the human cardiovascular system - the Hilbert transform (what we call the protophase) and the nonlinear protophase transform. The latter method allowed us to make the phase more linear, however, it did not significantly affect the coherence coefficient between the studied signals.

articleTitle: Analysis of EEG spectral amplitudes during ambiguous information processing
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We analyzed the dynamics of EEG spectral amplitudes in α- and β-frequency bands during ambiguous visual stimuli processing. As a result, we described differences in the cortical activity during the processing of visual stimuli with high and low ambiguity.

articleTitle: Development of features of the autonomic circulatory regulation in late premature and full term infants
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Objective: In this work, the development of the features of an autonomic system of blood circulatory regulation from the period of late prematurity to full-term infants is investigated using the example of signals of the photoplethysmogram of blood vessels, electrocardiogram, and respiration. The previous works of foreign and domestic authors show that interdependency between physiological rhythms emerges early in development. Much attention was paid to the study of cardiorespiratory coupling and his development in newborns, nevertheless, there are still many questions in this area. In this study, in addition to studying the standard low-frequency cardiorespiratory effect, we studied the relationships between the low-frequency components of the autonomic regulation of heart rate (using an electrocardiogram) and the tone of the arterial vessels (using photoplethysmogram of blood vessels). Approach: The goal of the work is to estimate the dynamics of the development of the coupling of the autonomic regulatory circuits of the cardiovascular system and respiratory system. In this paper, special attention is paid to the study of phase synchronization of these processes, as well as to the interaction of frequency components. We studied the coherence between heart rate variability, photoplethysmograms of blood vessels, and respiration signals of newborns with a gestational age of 30 weeks to 40 weeks. Main results: No significant changes in the measure of the estimation of phase synchronization with increases in the gestational age of the infant were found. The reason may be a notable change in the degree of connectedness of the studied systems after birth. There was also an assumption about the presence of changes in the direction of connectedness, but not in its strength. Significance: This study carries a fundamental interest - an understanding of the higher risk for negative results at the end of a premature population. Moreover, the continuation of work in this direction may allow creating a tool for the development of early markers of impaired autonomic regulation of the functions of the cardiovascular system and respiration in young children.

articleTitle: Network features of consolidated astrocytic response in modeled ischemia-like conditions in vitro
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Capability of astrocytes to regulate metabolic calcium activity without neuronal regulation and achieve a consolidated response is one of the most urgent tasks in modern neuroscience. This work is devoted the role of gap-contact in astrocytic consolidated responses under normal and ischemia-like conditions in vitro. In this study we investigated the cell viability in the postischemic period, main parameters of spontaneous calcium activity and the network characteristics of astrocytic cultures (average number of direct long-distant connections of single astrocyte and the rate of signal delay between astrocytes). Gap19 (100 μM) was used to estimate the role of connexin in the implementation of consolidated astrocytic response. We have shown that the network characteristics of astrocytic cultures are reduced in ischemia-like conditions. At the same time, the separation of astrocytic interactions by connexins 43 blockade can maintain cell viability and dynamic network characteristics in the post-ischemic period.

articleTitle: Transformation of the Theta-band Functional Connectivity During Motor Initiation Under Healthy Aging
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Human brain functioning is strongly affected by the factor of age, which crucially reduces a performance of the motor system. It causes a decline in reaction time, degraded ability to execute and control complex motor actions, low flexibility in learning new skills. A reduced daily activity old people combined with a cognitive and motor decline, usually result in a developed ambidexterity, i.e., the loss of a dominant limb advances. We suggest that such weakening of a dominant limb abilities and functioning on the neuronal level should be observed not only during the exact motor execution phase, but also in the motor initiation. In this paper we apply functional connectivity analysis to reveal the age-related changes in the integrative brain dynamic during the motor initiation before the dominant hand movements accompanied. Analyzing the whole-scalp electroencephalography (EEG) signals on the sensor level, we find higher theta-band coupling in the ipsilateral hemisphere.

articleTitle: Communication System Based on Chaotic Time-Delayed Feedback Generator
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We study communication systems based on chaotic time-delayed feedback generator. The aim of the study is a comparative assessment of the noise immunity for the four different communication systems at the same levels of the external noise. It is shown that the principle of correlation receiver, which is used in classical communication systems, can be also used in the case where chaotic signals generated by self-oscillating systems with complex behavior are used as reference signals. Systems based on the correlation receiver principles have very high immunity to the external noise.

articleTitle: Development of the approach to collaborative BCI
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In the present study we aim to find specific characteristic based on brain activity, that can be used to evaluate attention and, thus, can be used in brain-computer interface. We propose an approach to collaborative BCI aimed to enhance human-to-human interaction while performing shared visual task. We also describe the setup for such BCI and its possible application in long task of classifying ambiguous visual stimuli with varying degrees of ambiguity by a group of people.

articleTitle: Highest performance requires an optimal effort: A MEG study on visual perception
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Twelve subjects (6 males; 17-64 years) participated in magnetoencephalography (MEG) experiments designed to study visual response to flickering Necker cubes. Event-related fields in the lateral occipital complex and steady-state response in the visual region V1 and V2 were studied to characterise the early response time durations and attentional capacity during the trial time period of 5-s, respectively. We found that there was an optimal response time duration for which the attention capacity was maximum. The results also support the hypothesis that stimulus detection in brain is driven by coherence resonance.

articleTitle: Analysis of time lapse imaging of astrocyte calcium activity and reconstruction of astrocytic networks
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: One of the topical problems of neuroscience is understanding astrocyte calcium activity. Hypothetically, these cells form functional networks other than neural, that can process and produce information. In this study, we propose algorithms for the reconstruction of astrocytic networks based on time lapse of calcium activity.

articleTitle: The simplest oscillators with adaptive properties
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: We study the behavior of a non-autonomous oscillator with phase of the external force having the property of adaptability, i.e. depends on the dynamic variable. In the frame of this work we consider the case when dependence of the phase of external force is polynomial including terms of the third degree. Such dependence of the phase of the external action leads to the appearance of the complex chaotic oscillations in the dynamics of the oscillator. In the parameter space a hierarchy of various periodic and chaotic oscillations is observed. It is shown that in the dynamics of the system oscillation modes are observed, similar to the modes of a non-autonomous oscillator with a potential in the form of a periodic function. In the case of a linear adaptation function, the structure of the parameter plane has characteristic cascades of period doubling bifurcations. When nonlinearities (the second and the third terms of polynomial function) are taken into account, structures are destroyed.

articleTitle: Walking machines movement optimization with fuzzy nonlinear programming methods
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: There is shown an example of representation of problems of walking machines movement optimization to the form of convex optimization problems. Fuzzy formalization of convex optimization problems is proposed in relation to the designated problems of nonlinear programming.

articleTitle: Rearranging the coupling architecture in the brain in response to the introduction of various endocannabinoid receptor ligands
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: This study aims to reveal the connectivity rearrangement in the brain in response to the introduction of various endocannabinoid receptor ligands including both agonists and anthagonists. Rats of WAG/Rij and Wistar lines were investigated before and after introduction of WIN55,212-2 and SLV326 respectively. Local field potentials from different cortical areas, thalamic nuclei and hippocampus were recorded. Coupling analysis was performed using nonlinear Granger causality technique with models specially developed for the considered data. The results were statistically analyzed using ANOVA and t-test. Both coupling increase and decrease in different channel pairs was detected leading to complex evolution of brain network in time and causing the transition from baseline to seizure and between different types of epileptic activity.

articleTitle: Role of Pyramidal Cell M-current in Weak Pyramidal/Interneuronal Gamma Cluster Formation
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In the cortex gamma oscillations, generated in the networks consisting of pyramidal cells and interneurons, are typically irregular and sparse. Taking into account differences in the firing frequencies of pyramidal cells and interneurons, it is possible to conclude that a probable way of modelling of these gamma features is generation of the oscillations by alternating firing of the pyramidal cell clusters. Muscarine-sensitive potassium current (M-current) together with AHP-current plays important role in intrinsic dynamics of the pyramidal cells. In particular, it dampens the excitability (decreasing the spiking state range in the parameter space) and changes the excitability type of the pyramidal cells. These crucially act on the cluster formation process in the pyramidal subnetwork altering the number of clusters and, thus, coherence of the gamma rhythm.

articleTitle: On the Problem of Trajectory Tracking for Robotic Manipulators with Prismatic and Revolute Joints
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In this paper, a trajectory tracking control scheme for robot manipulators with prismatic and revolute joints is proposed using a new form of sliding modes. The stability analysis of the closed-loop system is carried out via Lyapunov function method. Compared to the conventional sliding mode control, our controller provides faster performance. Simulation results on a 5-degree-of-freedom robot arm demonstrate the applicability of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Network activity in primary hippocampal cultures upon HIF-prolyl hydroxylase inhibition
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The current study is aimed to determine the effect of HIF-prolyl hydroxylase inhibition on network characteristics of the functional calcium activity in primary hippocampal cultures in hypoxia model in vitro. We showed that inhibition of HIF prolyl hydroxylase during and immediately after hypoxia provides powerful support for the network activity of nervous cells and prevents destructive changes caused by hypoxia.

articleTitle: Network markers of DNA methylation in neurodegenerative diseases
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: One of the ways to reveal underlying complexity in high-dimensional data is a parenclitic network approach. Analysis of DNA methylation requires an understanding of interrelations between different genes that can be achieved through reconstructing unknown connectivity. In this paper, we identify network patterns that occur in DNA methylation of Down syndrome patients associated with aging and disease processes.

articleTitle: Analysis of algorithms for controlling the length of crawling robot modules
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: The paper proposes a control system for a crawling robot when it implements a flat motion while fixing the two extreme supports of the modules on the surface. Each module is a sliding pair of links, the modules are connected to each other by two active hinges that provide rotation of the modules in two mutually perpendicular planes. The contact of each module with the surface is made by means of two supports with a controlled coefficient of friction. A comparative analysis of three algorithms for controlling module lengths, which differ in the number of control stages and the number of controlled module lengths at each stage.

articleTitle: Global Limit Cycle Bifurcations of a Rational Kolmogorov Type System
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a quartic family of planar vector fields corresponding to a rational Kolmogorov type system which models the dynamics of the populations of predators and their prey in a given ecological or biomedical system and which is a variation on the classical Lotka-Volterra system. This family corresponds to the Leslie-Gower predator-prey model which uses the most common mathematical form of expressing the effect (or law) by Alle through the prey growth function. Applying the Wintner-Perko termination principle, we prove that the Leslie-Gower system with the Allee effect has at most two limit cycles surrounding one singular point.

articleTitle: Determination of responses to stimuli by the role of signal-triggering neurons in the network
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Visual stimulus discrimination ability of the brain means that somehow neuronal reaction has to differ concerning stimuli. We were interested in how we may find a nd describe the variation of neuronal response. We also wanted to pinpoint the structure of the neural network and functional interaction between its nodes. As a result, we propose a method for the characterization of neuronal response state to stimuli.

articleTitle: Ultra-fast method for solving the heat equation
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: This article is devoted to the numerical solution of heat equation. The main method of the work based on the assumption of the monotony of unknown function and parallel computations. In paper authors compares proposed method with classical methods. It is shown that the proposed method is easy to implement and can be applied to other differential equations of parabolic type.

articleTitle: Estimation of computational complexity for sub-optimal swarm control in non-cooperative games
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: A computational complexity is estimated for problem of a sub-optimal swarm control in a step-by-step strategy under limitation of a computing power. A general approach is used, for example, in competitions ¡¡Agar IO-like¿¿ for in-game AI makers on platform aicups.ru, organized by Mail.ru group.

articleTitle: Features of Neuron-Glial Networks Reorganiztion In Modeled Neurodegenerative Processes In Vitro
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: Features of neuron-glial networks reorganization in primary hippocampal cultures under chronic amyloid beta (Aβ) application have been studied. Primary hippocampal cultures were obtained from C57Bl/6 murine embryos and cultured during 21 days. The studies revealed the significant decrease in the key parameters characterizing connectivity of cells in a culture and simplification of functional neuron-glial networks.

articleTitle: Reconstructing the model of baroreflex control loop from short time series
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: An original method for reconstruction of time-delay systems parameters from time-series was tested on a radiophysical chaotic generator with quadratic nonlinearity and on a periodic radiophysical model of baroreflectory control of the mean arterial pressure. The method in question is based on analysis of synchronous response of the driven system. It was shown that parameters of chaotic generator can be reconstructed (the error is less than 1%) from a time-series which length was less than 2 delay times. The parameters of the periodic model were reconstructed from a time-series which length was 10 delay times.

articleTitle: Development of Natural Emotional Speech Database for Training Automatic Recognition Systems of Stressful Emotions in Human-Robot Interaction
publicationTitle: 2020 4th Scientific School on Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Application in Intellectual Robotics (DCNAIR)
abstract: A comparative analysis of 18 popular speech databases used in the field of affective computing was carried out. A database containing unique audio recordings of Russian speech (words, phrases, and sentences), registered in natural experience of emotions by eyewitnesses and/or participants in adverse events under stress, has been developed. Voice recordings were taken from video materials of disasters and emergencies occurred on the territory of Russia in 2015-2019. Examination results of psychological and psychiatric reactions of 293 eyewitnesses and/or participants (119 men and 174 women, aged 15 to 65 years) to traumatic factors of adverse events are presented. In accordance with the development results, the following key conclusions have been made: in the future, the database will allow researchers to objectively assess the capabilities of existing methods and approaches for analyzing emotional speech, as well as to assess the need for new mathematical devices in speech signal processing; the voice database can be successfully used as training or test sample, necessary for effective training of systems for automatic recognition of stressful emotions in human-robot interaction.
